chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did not leave the evening meal, even if it were just a cake, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is strength for the body.' And he said, and I do not know except that he said: 'And it is beneficial for intercourse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of eating the evening meal in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) emphasizes the consistent practice of consuming the evening meal, even minimally, framing it as a source of physical vitality and sexual health. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing bodily well-being as integral to spiritual and marital duties, reinforcing the Prophetic emphasis on maintaining strength for worship and family life.
